description: This topic teaches how to change direct speech into indirect (reported) speech, covering changes in pronouns, tenses and time/place words, the reporting of statements, questions, commands and requests, and the correct punctuation of direct speech.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence is written in direct speech?

options.text: She said that she was tired.
"I am tired," she said.
He told me he had finished.
They asked where I lived.

mcq.explanation: Direct speech repeats the speaker's exact words inside quotation marks. Option b quotes the words "I am tired" exactly.

mcq.questionText: Change to indirect speech: He said, "I am writing a letter."

options.text: He said that he was writing a letter.
He said that I am writing a letter.
He said that he is writing a letter.
He said that he wrote a letter.

mcq.explanation: The pronoun "I" becomes "he" and the present continuous "am writing" shifts back to the past continuous "was writing".

mcq.questionText: In reported speech, the word "today" usually changes to which of the following?

options.text: yesterday
that day
tomorrow
this day

mcq.explanation: Time words shift when reporting; "today" becomes "that day" because the words are reported at a later time.

mcq.questionText: Change to indirect speech: Asha said, "I will visit my aunt tomorrow."

options.text: Asha said that she will visit her aunt tomorrow.
Asha said that I would visit my aunt the next day.
Asha said that she would visit her aunt the next day.
Asha said that she would visit her aunt tomorrow.

mcq.explanation: "Will" becomes "would", "I/my" become "she/her", and "tomorrow" becomes "the next day".

mcq.questionText: Which is the correct reported form of the question: She asked, "Where do you live?"

options.text: She asked where do I live.
She asked where I lived.
She asked where did I live.
She asked where I live.

mcq.explanation: Reported wh-questions use statement word order (subject before verb) and no question mark; the present "live" becomes the past "lived".

mcq.questionText: Which verb correctly reports a yes/no question, as in: He asked, "Are you ready?"

options.text: He asked that I was ready.
He told if I was ready.
He asked whether I was ready.
He said whether I was ready.

mcq.explanation: Yes/no questions are reported with "if" or "whether" after "asked", and the verb shifts back to the past tense.

mcq.questionText: Change to indirect speech: The teacher said, "Open your books."

options.text: The teacher told us to open our books.
The teacher said that open your books.
The teacher asked to open our books.
The teacher told us that we open our books.

mcq.explanation: Commands are reported using "told" plus an object and an infinitive with "to"; "your" becomes "our".

mcq.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports a negative command: Mother said, "Don't touch the stove."

options.text: Mother said not to touch the stove.
Mother told me not to touch the stove.
Mother told me to don't touch the stove.
Mother said me not touch the stove.

mcq.explanation: A negative command is reported with "told" plus an object plus "not to" plus the base verb.

mcq.questionText: Change to indirect speech: "Please help me," the old man said to the boy.

options.text: The old man said the boy to help him.
The old man asked the boy please to help him.
The old man asked the boy to help him.
The old man told the boy that help me.

mcq.explanation: Polite requests are reported with "asked" plus an object plus an infinitive; the word "please" is dropped and "me" becomes "him".

mcq.questionText: What is the correct reported form of: She said, "I can swim very well."

options.text: She said that she can swim very well.
She said that she could swim very well.
She said that she would swim very well.
She said that she swam very well.

mcq.explanation: The modal verb "can" changes to "could" when the reporting verb is in the past tense.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence shows the correct punctuation of direct speech?

options.text: John said, "We are going home now."
John said "we are going home now".
John said, We are going home now.
"John said, we are going home now."

mcq.explanation: A comma follows the reporting verb, the spoken words begin with a capital letter, and the closing punctuation goes inside the quotation marks.

mcq.questionText: Change to indirect speech: Juma said, "I bought this book here."

options.text: Juma said that he had bought that book there.
Juma said that he bought this book here.
Juma said that I had bought that book there.
Juma said that he has bought that book here.

mcq.explanation: The simple past "bought" becomes the past perfect "had bought", "this" becomes "that", and "here" becomes "there".

mcq.questionText: Which is the correct reported form of: "Did you finish your homework?" the teacher asked Neema.

options.text: The teacher asked Neema if she finished her homework.
The teacher asked Neema if she had finished her homework.
The teacher asked Neema did she finish her homework.
The teacher asked Neema that she had finished her homework.

mcq.explanation: The yes/no question uses "if", the auxiliary "did" disappears, and the past tense shifts to the past perfect "had finished".

mcq.questionText: In which case does the tense usually NOT change when moving to indirect speech?

options.text: When the reporting verb is in the present tense.
When the sentence is a command.
When the sentence contains the word "tomorrow".
When the speaker uses the pronoun "I".

mcq.explanation: If the reporting verb is in the present tense (for example "he says"), the tense of the reported words stays the same.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct reported form: "I have been waiting for an hour," she complained.

options.text: She complained that she has been waiting for an hour.
She complained that she was waiting for an hour.
She complained that she had been waiting for an hour.
She complained that I had been waiting for an hour.

mcq.explanation: The present perfect continuous "have been waiting" shifts back to the past perfect continuous "had been waiting".

fib.questionText: He said, "I am hungry." In reported speech: He said that he _____ hungry.
fib.explanation: The present tense "am" changes to the past tense "was" because the reporting verb "said" is in the past.

fib.questionText: She said, "I will come tomorrow." In reported speech: She said that she would come the next _____.
fib.explanation: The time word "tomorrow" changes to "the next day" in reported speech.

fib.questionText: When reporting a command, we often use the reporting verb "told" followed by an object and the word "_____" before the verb.
fib.explanation: Commands are reported with the infinitive, for example "He told me to wait".

fib.questionText: The exact words a person speaks, written inside quotation marks, are called _____ speech.
fib.explanation: Direct speech records the speaker's exact words within quotation marks.

fib.questionText: They said, "We live here." In reported speech: They said that they lived _____.
fib.explanation: The place word "here" changes to "there" in reported speech.

fib.questionText: He asked, "Are you coming?" In reported speech: He asked _____ I was coming.
fib.explanation: Yes/no questions are reported using "if" or "whether".

fib.questionText: She said, "I saw him yesterday." In reported speech: She said that she _____ seen him the day before.
fib.explanation: The simple past "saw" becomes the past perfect "had seen" in reported speech.

fib.questionText: He said, "I can drive a car." In reported speech: He said that he _____ drive a car.
fib.explanation: The modal "can" changes to "could" in reported speech.

fib.questionText: The teacher said, "Don't make noise." In reported speech: The teacher told us _____ to make noise.
fib.explanation: Negative commands are reported with "not to" plus the base verb.

fib.questionText: She said, "I am studying now." In reported speech: She said that she was studying _____.
fib.explanation: The time word "now" changes to "then" in reported speech.

tf.questionText: Direct speech uses quotation marks to show the exact words of the speaker.
tf.explanation: Quotation marks enclose the speaker's exact words in direct speech.

tf.questionText: In indirect speech, quotation marks are still used around the reported words.
tf.explanation: Indirect speech does not use quotation marks because it reports the meaning, not the exact words.

tf.questionText: When the reporting verb is in the past tense, a present tense verb in the quoted words usually changes to the past tense.
tf.explanation: This backshift of tense happens because the words are reported later in the past.

tf.questionText: The word "now" changes to "yesterday" in reported speech.
tf.explanation: "Now" changes to "then", not "yesterday", in reported speech.

tf.questionText: A reported wh-question keeps the question word order, with the auxiliary verb placed before the subject.
tf.explanation: Reported questions use statement word order, with the subject coming before the verb.

tf.questionText: The word "please" is usually dropped when a request is changed into indirect speech.
tf.explanation: Politeness words like "please" are normally left out, and the reporting verb "asked" shows it was a request.

tf.questionText: A reported question ends with a question mark.
tf.explanation: An indirect question ends with a full stop because it is no longer a direct question.

tf.questionText: The pronoun "I" in direct speech may change to "he" or "she" in indirect speech depending on the speaker.
tf.explanation: Pronouns change to match the point of view of the person reporting the speech.

tf.questionText: If the reporting verb is in the present tense, the tense of the reported words usually does not change.
tf.explanation: No backshift is needed when the reporting verb is in the present, for example "She says she is tired".

tf.questionText: The modal verb "must", when expressing obligation, can stay as "must" or change to "had to" in reported speech.
tf.explanation: "Must" for obligation is often reported as "had to", though it can sometimes remain unchanged.

summary.correctAnswer: It is the speaker's exact words written inside quotation marks.
summary.explanation: Direct speech repeats the actual words spoken, for example: She said, "I am happy."

summary.correctAnswer: It reports what someone said without using their exact words or quotation marks.
summary.explanation: Indirect speech gives the meaning, for example: She said that she was happy.

summary.questionText: What happens to most present tense verbs when the reporting verb is in the past?
summary.correctAnswer: They shift back to the past tense.
summary.explanation: This is called backshifting, for example "am" becomes "was".

summary.questionText: How are statements reported in indirect speech?
summary.correctAnswer: By using a reporting verb such as "said" often followed by "that".
summary.explanation: Example: He said that he was tired.

summary.correctAnswer: By using "asked" with "if" or "whether" and statement word order.
summary.explanation: Example: She asked if I was ready.

summary.correctAnswer: By using "asked" plus the question word and statement word order, with no question mark.
summary.explanation: Example: He asked where I lived.

summary.correctAnswer: By using "told" plus an object plus an infinitive with "to".
summary.explanation: Example: The teacher told us to sit down.

summary.correctAnswer: By using "asked" plus an object plus an infinitive, dropping the word "please".
summary.explanation: Example: She asked me to close the door.

summary.questionText: Give an example of a time word change in reported speech.
summary.explanation: Other examples include "today" to "that day" and "now" to "then".

summary.questionText: What are the main punctuation rules for direct speech?
summary.correctAnswer: Use quotation marks around the spoken words, a comma after the reporting verb, and a capital letter to begin the speech.
summary.explanation: Example: Mother said, "Come here." The closing punctuation goes inside the quotation marks.

hoq.questionText: Report this sentence correctly: "I have been living in Mwanza since 2019," he explained.

options.text: He explained that he has been living in Mwanza since 2019.
He explained that he had been living in Mwanza since 2019.
He explained that I had been living in Mwanza since 2019.
He explained that he was living in Mwanza since 2019.

hoq.explanation: The present perfect continuous "have been living" shifts to the past perfect continuous "had been living", and "I" becomes "he".

hoq.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports a mixed command and reason: "Hurry up, because we are late!" the driver shouted.

options.text: The driver shouted to hurry up because we were late.
The driver shouted that hurry up because they were late.
The driver shouted at us to hurry up because they were late.
The driver shouted at us to hurry up because we are late.

hoq.explanation: The command becomes an infinitive ("to hurry up"), "we" becomes "they", and the present "are" shifts to the past "were".

hoq.questionText: Choose the correct reported form: She asked, "Why didn't you tell me about the meeting yesterday?"

options.text: She asked why I hadn't told her about the meeting the day before.
She asked why didn't I tell her about the meeting the day before.
She asked why I didn't tell her about the meeting yesterday.
She asked that why I hadn't told her about the meeting the day before.

hoq.explanation: The wh-question takes statement order, "didn't tell" becomes "hadn't told", "me" becomes "her", and "yesterday" becomes "the day before".
